chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and others from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
For Allah there is an Angel who records the extravagance in the Ablution just as he records his transgressions.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of wasting water during ablution in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the theological weight of *israf* (excess) in ritual purity, linking physical moderation to spiritual accountability. The hadith posits that a specific angel records the wastefulness of water during *wudu* just as it records acts of aggression (*udwan*), elevating ritual hygiene to a moral discipline. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that the manner of worship reflects one's consciousness of God, where even minor excesses in obligatory acts carry spiritual consequences.
